newsitem.title: UK: Merrill raises year-end FTSE 100 target to 5,000.
newsitem.headline: Merrill raises year-end FTSE 100 target to 5,000.

text.p: Merrill Lynch on Monday raised its year-end FTSE 100 target to 5,000 from 4,500 in line with a reduction in bond yield targets after last week's interest rate rise.

"Due to an increase in interest rate targets and a reduction in bond yield targets from 7.5 percent to 7.0 percent for the end of the year our FTSE fair-value target has increased in line," said UK equity strategist Philip Wolstencroft.

"We also have other technical factors in the market which are still very strong, such as director buying. Over the past four weeks on a moving average basis the director buying ratio is 2.5 percent, which is a pretty strong buy," Wolstencroft said.
"We still think there is room for growth alongside the market being at its peak...because we haven't got the technical signs that outline the introduction to a bear market."
